articles.title: Three clocks in one window at 1s, 5s and 30s, and not one component uses what the hook returns
articles.excerpt: Notifio is a desktop app whose UI exists to show the state of a background process: which searches are being watched, when each was last checked, how long it took, and what turned up. Almost every num…
articles.body: Notifio is a desktop app whose UI exists to show the state of a background process: which searches are being watched, when each was last checked, how long it took, and what turned up. Almost every number on screen is relative to now. "Last check 12s ago" is a lie four seconds later. There are two ways to deal with that. One is to store the formatted string and recompute it on an event. The other is to re-render on a timer and let the formatter read the clock. We do the second one, through a hook that is twelve lines long: /** * A clock that re-renders on an interval, so relative times and countdowns * stay honest without every component owning a timer.

articles.title: PDF to Word Without Breaking the Layout: A Translator's Workflow
articles.excerpt: PDF to Word Without Breaking the Layout: A Translator's Workflow “Can you convert this PDF to Word?” sounds like a five-minute job. It rarely is. A PDF is a picture of a document: the text may be embe…
articles.body: PDF to Word Without Breaking the Layout: A Translator's Workflow “Can you convert this PDF to Word?” sounds like a five-minute job. It rarely is. A PDF is a picture of a document: the text may be embedded, scanned, split into columns, or trapped inside text boxes. Converting it to Word is not a format change; it is a layout reconstruction. This is the workflow I use when a client sends a PDF that needs to become an editable Word file without losing tables, headers, footnotes or numbering. Step 1: Inspect the PDF before converting Open the PDF and check: Is the text selectable, or is it a scan? Is it one column or two? Are there tables, charts, footnotes or endnotes? Are there headers, footers and page numbers? Are there text boxes, sidebars or callouts? What fonts are embedded?

articles.title: Generate images by describing object positions in JSON — MOSS-Image walkthrough
articles.excerpt: Most image generation models understand prompts like "a red ball on the left and a blue cube on the right." The problem is, they understand it maybe half the time. The ball ends up on the right, or bo…
articles.body: Most image generation models understand prompts like "a red ball on the left and a blue cube on the right." The problem is, they understand it maybe half the time. The ball ends up on the right, or both objects merge into one, or the cube turns red too. Last week OpenMOSS released MOSS-Image, a 5B diffusion model under Apache 2.0 that addresses this with a different approach: describe object positions in JSON, and the model respects the coordinates. I put together a ComfyUI workflow and a prompt collection. Here's a walkthrough of how the JSON layout system works.

It's about a fundamental architectural question: Will the future of travel booking be a Super App — a single, all-in-one application where users search, book, and manage their travel, enhanced with AI features? articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built Every college WhatsApp group has the same problem: one message that matters ("Assignment 2 due Tuesday, 5 PM sharp") buried under three hundred memes and "ok sir"s. Miss it and you find out when someone asks why you didn't submit. Aalsi (Hindi for "lazy") is a deadline catcher for that. You export the group chat from WhatsApp (More → Export chat → Without media), drop the .txt file in, and it gives you: A morning digest: two plain lines ("0 due today, 1 tomorrow, 2 overdue") plus Today / Tomorrow / This Week lists. A "you may have missed" list for deadlines that already passed. A calendar file (.ics) you can import into any calendar app.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.

articles.title: Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise.'
articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.
